newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-FIVE-WICKET JOHNSON PUSHES FOR TEST PLACE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FIVE-WICKET JOHNSON PUSHES FOR TEST PLACE.

text.p: David Johnson gave a timely reminder to the Indian test selectors by taking five wickets on the opening day of a three-day match with Free State on Saturday.
Little medium-pacer Johnson took five for 78 in Free State's 320 for seven declared. India were 56 for one at the close.
He was dropped for the second test in Cape Town where India suffered their second successive defeat in the series. The third test starts in Johannesburg on Thursday.
It was another disappointing day for South African captain Hansie Cronje.
Cronje has been struggling for runs and showed no signs of a return to form before steering Johnson to second slip when he had made just four.
Cronje's dismissal plunged Free State into a crisis at 34 for three but 19-yar-old Boeta Dippenaar masterminded a fine recovery.
Dippenaar dominated a fourth-wicket stand of 178 with Chris Craven before falling four runs short of a well deserved century.
He hit 15 boundaries from 170 balls before playing a loose shot which gave a catch to second slip off Doda Ganesh.
With the score still on 212 Craven was brilliantly caught behind by Saba Karim for a hard-hit 76 which included six fours and a six.
But from 218 for six Kosie Venter took his side to the declaration with a well-crafted 54 not out from 84 balls with 10 boundaries.

In reply India's opening pair of Workeri Raman and Vikram Rathore put the Free State attack to the sword. But in the penultimate over of the day Raman miscued a pull against Bradley Player and was caught behind.
Raman contributed 18 to an opening stand of 52. At the close Rathore was on 33 with night-watchman Venkatapathy Raju on nought.
